newsitem.title: USA: First United, Fredonia merge for $62 mln.
newsitem.headline: First United, Fredonia merge for $62 mln.

text.p: First United Bancshares Inc said Tuesday it has a letter of intent to merge with Fredonia Bancshares Inc, a $245 million banking company in Texas, in a deal valued at about $62 million.

First United said it will exchange about 1.6 million shares of its common stock for all the 472,324 Fredonia shares outstanding. The total purchase price is about $131 per share for each Fredonia share, First United said.

Fredonia is the parent company of Fredonia State Bank, Nacogdoches, Texas. Its 1996 net income was $4.1 million and its total deposits were $217 million, with loans of $123 million, First United said.
First United said Fredonia will be the third largest bank in its group.

"We are very comfortable with and supportive of Fredonia's present mode of operation. Their history of community service, shareholder returns and outstanding management and staff make it an ideal fit with First United and our banks," First United said in a release.
The deal requires approval from Fredonia shareholders and regulatory authorities. It should close in the third quarter.
First United has $1.5 billion in assets and eleven subsidiary banks in Arkansas and Texas.
